h: פָּרָשַׁת כִּי תֵצֵא, ד׳ Ki Seitzei, 4
Removing Evil Until Its Root Cannot Return

p: "And you shall remove the evil from your midst":
it is merely like a translation
of what is written in the Torah
so what did the Sifrei add with this?
"And you shall remove the evil from your midst"
that when they remove the sinner
and all who are executed confess
to rectify the corruption at the root,
which at its beginning was in eating,
And this is the meaning of
"And you shall remove the evil from your midst (mikirbecha)":
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמַר בַּגְּמָרָא (תַּעֲנִית יא, ב)
along the lines of what the Gemara says (Taanis 11b):
'In your midst is the Holy One'";
And it uses the word "u'viarta, remove";
and it says in the Gemara (Bava Kamma 2b):
וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר (מְלָכִים א יד, י)
'As one removes dung, until it is all gone.'"
trampling with its foot and damaging it,
which is not so of damage by the tooth,
which consumes it until it is all gone,
"And you shall remove the evil from your midst":
that he rectifies to the root
"as one removes until it is all gone,"
And the Sifrei added with this,
that this refers to the present:
that he should remove in the present
to rectify the root of the corruption,
that is, that the yetzer hara
as at the Giving of the Torah,
when the yetzer hara returned to its place.
Now there are mentioned in Mishneh Torah
the expression "And you shall remove the evil"
in the passage of the false prophet;
and five times in this parashah.
corresponding to the aspect of Knesses Yisrael,
"ten utterances for the Giving of the Torah,
ten utterances for the work of Creation"
corresponds to the tribe of Yehudah
who will be of his seed,
when the evil will be removed
although one removes the evil from Yisrael,
it is only as at the Giving of the Torah:
that at the utterance "You shall not have"
the yetzer hara was uprooted from Yisrael,
the yetzer hara returned to its place.
Which is not so in the future,
then the yetzer hara will be nullified completely,
for HaKadosh Baruch Hu will slaughter
that "And you shall remove the evil," etc.
in the passage of the false prophet,
"After Hashem your God shall you walk," etc.;
and there are six expressions in it,
and after this it is written:
"And you shall remove the evil from your midst";
for the souls of the seven shepherds
"After Hashem your God shall you walk"
Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
who began, by his own effort,
to publicize the Kingdom of Heaven in the world,
and it was said to him (Bereishis 17:1):
And this is what the Sifrei says there:
"'After Hashem your God shall you walk'
and this is the attribute of
who was the aspect of alacrity,
that is what it comes to teach us;
(Rashi on the Rif, chapter 1 of Avodah Zarah);
Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
and this is what the Sifrei says:
Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
whose attribute is the attribute of truth,
"The lip of truth shall be established forever."
And this is why it says "you shall keep":
"And to His voice shall you listen"
Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
who brought down the words of Torah,
which is the aspect of voice,
the voices at the Giving of the Torah
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רסא, א)
who is the root of the service,
in the service of the korbanos.
"For the lips of a kohen," etc.,
"and they shall seek Torah from his mouth";
Aharon HaKohen was the one who served.
the aspect of the small vav,
and through him is the connection:
"who holds on to heaven and earth,"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק א לא, א)
And this is what it says:
to the vav shall you cleave;
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דְּבָרִים ד, ד)
and this is in the manner of what it says (Devarim 4:4):
from the passage of this wicked man:
meaning that he cast filth into her
(similar to what it says in Yevamos 103b),
and this is through the attribute of
"And you shall remove the evil from your midst";
and this corresponds to the aspect of
David HaMelech, peace be upon him,
who raised up the yoke of teshuvah
the yetzer hara is completely uprooted,
as at the Giving of the Torah;
that the yetzer hara will return to its place,
after the Giving of the Torah.
and this is in all ten attributes,
which is written in this parashah
kidnapping a person from Yisrael," etc.,
all the evil deed he did,
and so his deeds are nullified
"and he treats him as a slave"
and especially the person, who is returned.
And then his death will help
"And you shall remove the evil from your midst,"
to rectify everything to the root
And this is what the Sifrei says:
for whose sake the whole world
by the power of his teshuvah,
will bring a thought of teshuvah
in the passage of the kidnapper,
for it is in monetary law.
This is not so of all the other sins:
for even though he did teshuvah
nevertheless the lust of its moment
where all his deeds were nullified.
the death of the thief helps:
the yetzer hara will be nullified
and this will be in the days of Mashiach,
it is written the eleventh time,
from the accusation of the yetzer hara,
and in the Mechilta the wording is
that he is guarded from sin,
from the accusation of the yetzer hara.
And one who merits the upper Shabbos
from him the yetzer hara is cleared out
in the two chambers of the heart,
and there is cleared out from there
as in the days of Mashiach
and in the World to Come.
